messages.notebook.note.START_ROUTINE: I have some savings to begin slowly and get to know people, but they are not a regular income. I need to allow for food, weekly home rent to Uncle Abdel Karim and kiosk rent to the district. Dates are in the accounts pages.
messages.notebook.note.WORKSHOP_OPPORTUNITY: Farid needs someone to help with simple workshop tasks and learn along the way. Usually three afternoons a week.
messages.notebook.note.YOUSSEF_WORK_STUDY: Youssef is looking for work around his studies. He has two days free after lectures.
messages.notebook.note.WORK_TRIAL_APPOINTMENT: Farid and Youssef arranged a workshop trial together. I heard the appointment details from them.
messages.notebook.note.WORK_TRIAL_RESULT: Youssef really did try working at the workshop. The tasks and working together seemed a good fit; continuing depends on agreeing the days.
messages.notebook.note.WORK_TRIAL_WEEK: Farid and Youssef agreed on a week’s trial, working two days around his studies.
messages.notebook.note.KNOWN_CHEAP_FAN: Amgad pointed me to a second-hand standing fan at Uncle Saeed’s. I can order it from the kiosk phone.
messages.notebook.note.KNOWN_ABDUL_FAMILY: Uncle Abdel Karim visits his mother every day. It matters to him that someone checks in on him too.
messages.notebook.note.KNOWN_SHAWARMA_BASICS: Shawarma: prepare on a worktop, marinate in the local fridge, cook on the spit, then slice and assemble with bread and garlic sauce. The equipment and ingredients really are needed.

messages.story.amgad.line_001: Evening, son. A cup of tea whenever you're ready. We've got time to sit.
messages.story.amgad.line_002: Lovely evening! Thought I'd stop for tea by the Nile before heading home.
messages.story.amgad.line_003: How are you, son? Finally done at the office. Put the kettle on for me.
messages.story.amgad.line_004: Good evening, everyone. A cup of tea while I rest my feet a bit.
messages.story.amgad.line_005: Thank you. When you've got a moment, I've got a lead on a fan for your rooftop room.
messages.story.amgad.line_006: Lovely. This deserves to be sipped slowly.
messages.story.amgad.line_007: Beautiful. The smell of the tea alone wakes you up.
messages.story.amgad.line_008: Now we're all set. Thank you, son.
messages.story.amgad.line_009: Never mind. We'll get it right next time. Looks like you've had a long day.
messages.story.amgad.line_010: I'm Amgad. I work in the office at the end of the street. I stop here to unwind before going home.
messages.story.amgad.line_012: Bless you. Sitting here lets you forget the traffic for a while.
messages.story.amgad.line_013: Hope work goes easy on you.
messages.story.amgad.line_014: And on you, son. We're all just trying to get home with a little peace left.
messages.story.amgad.line_016: The water's a nicer sound than telephones ringing all day.
messages.story.amgad.line_017: Uncle Said, the electrician behind the station, has a good secondhand pedestal fan for {fan_price_label} pounds. Tell him I sent you. You can order it from the kiosk phone.
messages.story.amgad.line_018: Thanks. That rooftop room really is hot at night.
messages.story.amgad.line_019: Hope it brings you a good night's sleep.
messages.story.amgad.line_020: Once I've saved up for it, God willing.
messages.story.amgad.line_021: Take your time, son. There's no rush.
messages.story.amgad.line_022: I heard the fan arrived! How's sleeping up on the roof now?
messages.story.amgad.line_023: It's made a real difference. Thanks for the tip.
messages.story.amgad.line_024: Enjoy it, son. A bit of comfort at home is what matters.
messages.story.amgad.line_026: Give it time. Uncle Said's nearby if you need anything.
messages.story.amgad.line_027: That tea you made last time was just right. I was still thinking about it at the office.
messages.story.amgad.line_028: Remember that last cup? Don't worry about it. Every day's different.
messages.story.amgad.line_029: Good to see you, my friend. I can spot you in your usual place from a mile off now.
messages.story.amgad.line_030: Street's busy right now. I'll wait a bit for it to quiet down.
messages.story.amgad.line_031: Best time of day, when the sun goes down and the breeze starts coming through.
messages.story.amgad.line_032: A day of paperwork and figures. Let's look at the water for two minutes without counting anything.
messages.story.amgad.line_033: The barber's had his radio on since morning. That song's still going round my head.
messages.story.football.line_001: The ref ruined yesterday's match, Samir!
messages.story.football.line_002: Oh, come on. Your lot were asleep the whole second half!
messages.story.football.line_003: Did you hear the post-match show? Two hours talking about one goal!
messages.story.football.line_004: Well, if the defence had been awake, we'd have settled it ages ago.
messages.story.football.line_005: I'd love to go watch at the stadium for once, instead of the café.
messages.story.football.line_006: You go. I like watching the match and getting home without the crowds.
messages.story.football.line_007: As long as we can still enjoy sitting together.
messages.story.football.line_008: You're right, boss. The football ends, but the friendship stays.
messages.story.football.line_009: That's the spirit. Let's enjoy ourselves here.
messages.story.football.line_010: Give the football a rest and enjoy the breeze.
messages.story.football.line_011: Honestly, this breeze beats any match.
messages.story.football.line_012: All right, all right. Let's take a breather.
messages.story.football.line_014: Enough, Mahmoud. Let's drink our tea before it gets cold.
messages.story.football.line_015: I came for the company anyway. Forget the match.
messages.story.venue_comments.line_001: Mind the floor, boss. It could do with a clean.
messages.story.venue_comments.line_002: That seat needs a wipe before anyone sits down.
messages.story.venue_comments.line_003: The prep area here could use a bit more cleaning.
messages.story.venue_comments.line_004: Place is cleaner than last time I came. You've clearly been looking after it.
messages.story.venue_comments.line_005: I still remember the {venue_previous_food} I had last time. That was good.
messages.story.venue_comments.line_006: I remember the {venue_previous_food} I had here. It needed a little work. Shall we try for better this time?
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_001: A relative of mine worked in a shawarma shop. He used to tell me: prep the chicken and marinade on a worktop, chill the bowl, then it's the spit, slicing, and putting it all together.
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_002: So what do I need to set up?
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_003: A shawarma spit set in place, a clear worktop, and a working fridge. Chicken and marinade in the fridge, oil and bread in storage, and chilled toum. Each bit of equipment has its own job.
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_004: How do I know when it's finished marinating?
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_005: Leave the bowl in the fridge for the time it needs. Holding it doesn't count as chilling. Then fetch it yourself and load the spit.
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_006: Right. I'll get the place ready and give it a go.
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_007: Take your time, and leave the filling alone till it's cooked. I'll stop by again and hear how you got on.
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_008: You've started trying out shawarma, then? Good on you for having a go. If you're halfway through, check where the bowl is and how long each step takes before rushing into the next.
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_009: That's an excellent shawarma sandwich! Looks like you got the steps and timing right this time.
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_010: That came out well. Keep the marinating right, and watch your slicing and assembly times on the next try.
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_011: It's edible, but there's still room to improve. Look at whichever step went worst in that batch. Putting the sandwich together won't rescue filling that's been left too long.
messages.story.shawarma_learning.line_012: Did it burn? It happens. Watch the time on the spit and turn the heat off instead of leaving the rest of the batch on it.
messages.story.visitors.line_001: Good evening. A liver sandwich to take home, please.
messages.story.visitors.line_002: How's it going, boss? One liver sandwich for the road. I'll be out of your way.
messages.story.visitors.line_003: Just left my sister's. Thought I'd pick up dinner from you.
messages.story.visitors.line_004: Workshop's shut for the day. A liver sandwich while I stand here and give my back a rest.
messages.story.visitors.line_005: One liver sandwich, chief. My hands ache from work. Can't face cooking.
messages.story.visitors.line_006: Evening. Make me a sandwich to keep me going on the way home.
messages.story.visitors.line_007: Evening again. Thought I'd have tea here instead of all the bustle at home.
messages.story.visitors.line_008: Evening. Today I'd like a cup of tea with no exercise books and no marking.
messages.story.visitors.line_009: Hello, boss. Saw an empty chair and took it as a sign. Tea, please.
messages.story.visitors.line_010: I'm Salma. I teach at the school just behind here. A cup of tea and a little sit-down, please.
messages.story.visitors.line_011: A cup of tea, boss. I'll go over a couple of pages before heading home.
messages.story.visitors.line_012: Evening. Tea while I wait for my friend, if he remembers to turn up!
messages.story.visitors.line_013: Finally dragged ourselves through the lectures. Time for a leisurely tea.
messages.story.visitors.line_014: That's lovely. At this rate it'll be gone before I get home.
messages.story.visitors.line_015: Thanks, chief. Let's eat before anyone remembers there's work to do.
messages.story.visitors.line_016: Smells lovely. A little moment to myself.
messages.story.visitors.line_017: Now I can open the book. Or try to, anyway.
messages.story.visitors.line_018: Well, I might as well stay another couple of minutes. Thanks.
messages.story.visitors.line_019: Bless you. You've saved me cooking tonight.
messages.story.visitors.line_020: Bless you. Beats eating dinner alone in the workshop.
messages.story.visitors.line_021: Thank you. Tea with this breeze is something else.
messages.story.visitors.line_022: Thanks. Couldn't ask for anything more now.
messages.story.visitors.line_023: Lovely. Thanks for going to the trouble.
messages.story.visitors.line_024: Thank you. That's dinner sorted. See you soon.
messages.story.visitors.line_025: Lovely, chief. Just the way to finish a day at the workshop.
messages.story.visitors.line_026: Thank you. I'll drink it before I look at those exercise books.
messages.story.visitors.line_027: Just what I needed. Might get my brain working!
messages.story.visitors.line_028: Thank you. I'll sip it while I look across the river.
messages.story.visitors.line_029: A cup to settle the nerves after that match.
messages.story.visitors.line_030: Thanks, boss. Let's have dinner and forget football for a bit.
messages.story.visitors.line_032: Thanks. Maybe a little adjustment next time.
messages.story.visitors.line_033: Thanks, boss. We all have our days.
messages.story.visitors.line_034: Bless you. Catch your breath too if it's been a hard day.
messages.story.visitors.line_035: Take your time. Just remember my order when you're free.
messages.story.visitors.line_036: Still remember me, boss? I'm over here.
messages.story.visitors.line_037: If you've run out of ingredients, just say. It's all right.
messages.story.visitors.line_038: The tea was just right last time. That's why I thought I'd stop by again.
messages.story.visitors.line_039: The tea wasn't quite to my taste last time. Let's give it another go today.
messages.story.visitors.line_040: That sandwich last time was good. Thought of it as I was passing.
messages.story.visitors.line_041: The last sandwich needed a little work, but we all have tiring days.
messages.story.visitors.line_042: See that little felucca? It was by the bridge just a moment ago.
messages.story.visitors.line_043: The breeze here beats our balcony today.
messages.story.visitors.line_044: Just another couple of minutes, then I'll head home.
messages.story.visitors.line_045: The Nile has a different sort of grandeur at night.
messages.story.visitors.line_046: Boats are still out working. May everyone earn a good living.
messages.story.visitors.line_047: Breeze has changed. Looks like it'll be a nicer night.
messages.story.visitors.line_048: Ten minutes on the same page. I think studying's over for today.
messages.story.visitors.line_049: When my friend says five minutes, he means half an hour.
messages.story.visitors.line_050: Might take a little walk instead of staring at these papers.
messages.story.visitors.line_051: The Nile breeze brings you back to life after a long day.
messages.story.visitors.line_052: Good evening to everyone taking it easy.
messages.story.visitors.line_053: A little stroll along the Corniche, then home.
messages.story.visitors.line_054: I'm Nadia. I live in the street behind here. Sometimes I stop by on my way back from my sister's.
messages.story.visitors.line_055: Been rushing about since morning. Finally found ten minutes to myself.
messages.story.visitors.line_056: You can smell the food right down the street. May business be good.
messages.story.visitors.line_057: I'm Farid, from the workshop. Engines clattering all day. Here you can hear yourself think.
messages.story.visitors.line_058: Changed a car's fan belt today. Got home and found my own fan had stopped!
messages.story.visitors.line_059: One of these days I'll shut the workshop early. I'd love to catch the sunset for once.
messages.story.visitors.line_060: Our last lesson today was drawing the Nile. Every child sees it differently.
messages.story.visitors.line_061: I'll mark the books later. I don't have to take school everywhere with me.
messages.story.visitors.line_062: One of the kids drew the boat bigger than the bridge. Maybe he's got a point!
messages.story.visitors.line_063: I'm Mona, your neighbour from down the street. Not ordering anything. I just like standing by the railing a while.
messages.story.visitors.line_064: Went out for bread and took the long way round so I could pass by here.
messages.story.visitors.line_065: No more errands today. A little time to ourselves.
messages.story.visitors.line_066: I'm Youssef. I'm at university. The paperwork doesn't feel as heavy here as it does in my room.
messages.story.visitors.line_067: There's still time before the exam. That's what I'm trying to tell myself, anyway.
messages.story.visitors.line_068: Once exams are over, I'm coming here without this bag for once.
messages.story.visitors.line_069: People call me Mr Hassan, though I stopped working years ago. The name just stuck.
messages.story.visitors.line_070: Used to pass here on my way to work. Now I come whenever I like.
messages.story.visitors.line_071: I like somewhere you can sit without having to talk the whole time.
messages.story.visitors.line_072: Samir and I disagree on everything except sitting here.
messages.story.visitors.line_073: Don't listen to Samir about football. We've been friends since school, though.
messages.story.visitors.line_074: Let's stick to tea. Football's done enough to our nerves.
messages.story.visitors.line_075: If Mahmoud's team loses, he'll blame anything except the team.
messages.story.visitors.line_076: I come for the company and the food. The football argument just turns up on its own.
messages.story.visitors.line_077: Heading home early today. Got somewhere to be in the morning.
messages.story.visitors.line_078: Street's still busy. The Nile breeze beats standing at the traffic lights.
messages.story.visitors.line_079: A stroll along the Corniche before home. Need a little time to unwind.
messages.story.companionship.001: The breeze here really loosens up your back after a day at the workshop. Got time for a chat?
messages.story.companionship.002: You come here to hear the water instead of your own thoughts. Got a minute?
messages.story.companionship.004: Sorry, I need a little time to myself.
messages.story.companionship.005: No worries, my friend. There's room here for all of us.
messages.story.companionship.007: Whenever you like. There's no rush.
messages.story.companionship.008: I'm Farid. I've got a workshop nearby. I come down to the Nile to stretch my back. You don't have to be doing something every minute.
messages.story.companionship.009: It's a blessing, sitting here. We can get to know each other little by little.
messages.story.companionship.010: Youssef. I'm at university, still figuring things out. I like walking here after lectures, away from the noise.
messages.story.companionship.011: It's nice having somewhere you can be quiet without anyone asking what's wrong.
messages.story.companionship.012: Remember the workshop I told you about? I could use someone to sort the tools and help with small jobs. I'd teach them as we go.
messages.story.companionship.013: Usually it's three afternoons a week, but we can talk about what works for them. We'd try it first; I can't promise a job.
messages.story.companionship.014: Honestly, I'm looking for work alongside my studies. Expenses are getting heavy, but I don't want to leave university.
messages.story.companionship.015: I can manage two days after lectures. Any more and my studies would suffer. That's why I'm taking my time asking around.
messages.story.companionship.016: Youssef's looking for work? Glad you thought of us. We could talk about a short trial and see whether the work suits him.
messages.story.companionship.017: Farid wants someone to learn at his workshop? That could be a good start, but let me ask what the work involves first.
messages.story.companionship.018: Only two days because of university? We can try two days. Teaching takes patience, and I'm happy for his studies to come first.
messages.story.companionship.019: Shall I tell him you're happy with two days?
messages.story.companionship.020: Yes, tell him. If the trial goes well, we can carry on for a trial week on those two days.
messages.story.companionship.021: Let me check his schedule and get back to you.
messages.story.companionship.022: Take your time. The hours need to work for him too.
messages.story.companionship.023: Farid's happy with two days? Then I can keep up with lectures and try the work without taking on too much.
messages.story.companionship.024: Shall I tell him it's two days, if the trial works for you both?
messages.story.companionship.025: Yes, I'm happy with that. A trial week of two days if the tasks suit us. One step at a time.
messages.story.companionship.026: Sort out your schedule first. Take your time.
messages.story.companionship.027: Thanks. I'll check my university timetable.
messages.story.companionship.028: Youssef and I have spoken. We've arranged a trial {appointment_label}. If either of us is still here, we'll finish sitting and sort out the start without rushing.
messages.story.companionship.029: We've been in touch and arranged a trial {appointment_label}. I'll get to know the tools and try some simple jobs, then we'll see.
messages.story.companionship.030: We're still sorting out a time. I've agreed to get in touch, but nothing's settled yet. We'll tell you when it is.
messages.story.companionship.031: We're still arranging it together. Agreeing to talk doesn't mean the trial has happened. One thing at a time.
messages.story.companionship.032: Youssef came to the workshop and we gave it a go. We started by sorting the tools and going over simple jobs together. He asks questions and listens, which is reassuring.
messages.story.companionship.033: We still need to agree on regular days so his studies don't suffer. The trial itself was a good start.
messages.story.companionship.034: I went to the workshop. At first I worried I'd mix up the tools, but Farid let me try things slowly and ask all the questions I wanted.
messages.story.companionship.035: The tasks seem suitable so far, but we still need to agree on days around university. Trying the work doesn't mean I've left my studies.
messages.story.companionship.036: If it suits you, could he contact you to arrange a trial?
messages.story.companionship.037: Yes, I'm happy for him to contact me so we can arrange a trial. We'll get in touch away from our time here and see what works.
messages.story.companionship.038: Let me ask him first, without promising anything.
messages.story.companionship.039: Of course. We shouldn't make promises on someone else's behalf.
messages.story.companionship.040: Would you like to get in touch and try the work first?
messages.story.companionship.041: Yes, let's get in touch and arrange a trial. Tell him I'm interested, but I'm still learning about the work. I'm not agreeing to a permanent schedule yet.
messages.story.companionship.042: Think it over. There's no obligation.
messages.story.companionship.043: Thanks. Let's come back to it when I've had time to think.
messages.story.companionship.044: We've agreed on a trial week of two days. We'll teach and learn, and make room for university. It's still a trial, with no promise of a lasting job.
messages.story.companionship.045: The two days worked around my lectures, so we've agreed on a trial week. I'm glad I can take a step forward without leaving my studies. Thanks for looking out for me.
messages.story.landlord.001: Good evening, son. How are you? If you've got a moment, let's sit down and calmly go over what we owe each other.
messages.story.landlord.002: Here's the rent for my room: {housing_due_label} pounds.
messages.story.landlord.003: Thank you, son. Here's your receipt. It's all recorded clearly in the ledger.
messages.story.landlord.004: I can pay {partial_label} pounds now, and we can discuss the rest.
messages.story.landlord.005: All right. I'll record just what I've received. We still need to agree on the remainder.
messages.story.landlord.006: Could we agree on more time for the rent? I'm sorting out my priorities and need to settle on a date.
messages.story.landlord.007: Let's agree on a date we can keep, not just say the words.
messages.story.landlord.010: I can sort it out within a week.
messages.story.landlord.011: Let me think first. I don't want to promise something I'm unsure of.
messages.story.landlord.012: Take your time. Without a new agreement, the original amount is still due as before.
messages.story.landlord.013: How do things stand with my rent?
messages.story.landlord.014: Everything you've paid has a receipt, and your next due date is in your ledger. I won't take money from you without a proper record.
messages.story.landlord.015: Could I borrow some money and repay the principal on a date we agree on?
messages.story.landlord.016: I can help within my means. Let's agree on the amount and the term first.
messages.story.landlord.020: Sorry, let me sort things out first.
messages.story.landlord.021: No worries. We haven't agreed on a loan yet.
messages.story.landlord.022: I'm sorry, son. Lending money is a responsibility, and I can't promise you money right now. You're still welcome to talk things through with me.
messages.story.landlord.023: Here's the remaining loan principal: {loan_remaining_label} pounds.
messages.story.landlord.024: I've received it. May things get easier for you. Your receipt is saved, and there's nothing added to the principal.
messages.story.landlord.025: I'm sorry I didn't keep the date I promised you.
messages.story.landlord.026: I appreciate you coming to talk. Your apology matters. Let's clearly arrange repayment or a new agreement.
messages.story.landlord.028: And how are you? How's life treating you?
messages.story.landlord.029: She's more settled today, thank God. We sat together for a while, and my sister stopped by. Thanks for remembering.
messages.story.landlord.030: She still needs rest, but she's started calling to ask why I'm late. Hearing her like that puts my mind at ease.
messages.story.landlord.031: I visited her before coming here. She asked me to bring some old newspapers, and we sat remembering old stories.
messages.story.landlord.032: I'm all right, thank God. My mother hasn't been well, and I try to visit her every day. Sometimes all you need is someone to ask how you're doing.
messages.story.landlord.033: I hope she gets better soon. Let me know if you need anything.
messages.story.landlord.037: Let's carry on another time, Uncle.
messages.story.landlord.038: Whenever you like. I'll stay a little longer, then head off.
messages.story.landlord.039: I can wait until {extension_1_date}. If you agree, that's our new promise. The original amount stays the same.
messages.story.landlord.040: Shall we agree on {extension_3_date}? The amount remains due, but that becomes the date we've promised each other.
messages.story.landlord.041: I can wait until {extension_7_date}. Let's be clear so we can both plan ahead.
messages.story.landlord.042: Agreed. That's a date I can promise.
messages.story.landlord.043: We've agreed on {agreed_date}. The agreement is recorded, and the original amount due stays on the books.
messages.story.landlord.044: No, I can't promise that. Let's leave it without a new agreement.
messages.story.landlord.045: All right. Offering more time doesn't mean you've made a promise.
messages.story.landlord.046: I can lend you {loan_0_label} pounds. Repay the same principal {loan_duration_label} after you receive it, with nothing added.
messages.story.landlord.047: I can lend you {loan_1_label} pounds. Repay the same principal {loan_duration_label} after you receive it, with nothing added.
messages.story.landlord.048: I can lend you {loan_2_label} pounds. Repay the same principal {loan_duration_label} after you receive it, with nothing added.
messages.story.landlord.049: I agree to the amount and the term. I'll repay the same principal.
messages.story.landlord.050: Here you go. You've received the money, and the repayment date and receipt are saved in the ledger.
messages.story.landlord.051: Thank you, but I won't take the loan right now.
messages.story.landlord.052: No worries. No money has changed hands, and no debt has been recorded.
messages.story.orders.001: When you've got a moment, son, make me {order_label}. No rush.
messages.story.orders.002: Please, boss, I'd like {order_label} before I head home.
messages.story.orders.003: Make us {order_label}, chief, while I give my back a rest.
messages.story.orders.004: Could I have {order_label}, please? Sitting here gives you an appetite.
messages.story.orders.005: {order_label}, boss. Might wake my brain up a bit.
messages.story.orders.006: Could I trouble you for {order_label}? We're in no hurry.
messages.story.orders.007: One {order_label}, my friend. Maybe it'll calm Samir down.
messages.story.orders.009: Good evening. Could I have {order_label} whenever you're ready?
messages.story.orders.010: No worries, son. I ordered {order_label}. Take your time.
messages.story.orders.011: Hope your day's going all right. {order_label}, dear. I'm in no hurry.
messages.story.orders.012: {order_label}, son. Sometimes I forget why I walked into a room!
messages.story.orders.014: {order_label}, please. Mind you, I've forgotten what I came to buy at the market too.
messages.story.orders.015: No worries. {order_label}. Keep up the good work.
messages.story.orders.016: {order_label}, chief. Don't send us back to the workshop hungry!
messages.story.orders.017: No worries. I ordered {order_label}. Your head gets crowded sometimes.
messages.story.orders.018: {order_label}, my friend. Don't worry, I still remember!
messages.story.orders.020: {order_label}, please. I won't be testing you on it!
messages.story.orders.021: Hang in there. {order_label}, whenever you're ready.
messages.story.orders.022: {order_label}, boss. Good to know I'm not the only one who forgets!
messages.story.orders.023: I ordered {order_label}. If that comes up on the exam, I'll pass.
messages.story.orders.024: No worries. Just {order_label}. Take your time.
messages.story.orders.025: {order_label}, son. Better to ask than guess.
messages.story.orders.027: Memory's a funny thing. {order_label}, and good health to you.
messages.story.orders.028: {order_label}, my friend. Samir's chatter must have thrown you off!
messages.story.orders.029: I ordered {order_label}. Remembered it without a slow-motion replay, too.
messages.story.orders.030: {order_label}, whenever you're ready. We're still debating.
messages.story.orders.031: {order_label}, boss. Don't listen if Mahmoud tells you otherwise.
messages.story.orders.032: No worries. I ordered {order_label}. You need patience with us!
messages.story.orders.033: {order_label}, my friend. I still remember the taste from last time.
messages.story.orders.037: {order_label}, when you're free. I'll be here a while yet.
messages.story.orders.038: Catch your breath, boss. I'm happy to wait for {order_label}.
messages.story.orders.039: If {order_label} isn't available right now, just tell me. No problem.
messages.story.service_availability.001: When you've got a moment, could I have {order_label}? No rush.
messages.story.service_availability.002: I'll be sitting here a while. Could you make me {order_label}?
messages.story.service_availability.003: How's it going, boss? I'd love {order_label}, if that's possible.
messages.story.service_availability.004: Are you open, boss? The sign says closed, but I thought I'd ask. Could I get {order_label}?
messages.story.service_availability.005: Closed up, boss? Taking a break? If it's no trouble, could I have {order_label}?
messages.story.service_availability.006: I don't want to interrupt your break. If you can make {order_label}, I'm happy to wait.
messages.story.service_availability.007: Of course. I'll make it for you.
messages.story.service_availability.008: Thanks, my friend. I'm in no hurry.
messages.story.service_availability.009: I was clearing my head for a bit. Sorry, let's leave it till later.
messages.story.service_availability.010: No worries. Take your time. It's nice sitting here even without ordering anything.
messages.story.service_availability.011: I need to get supplies first. I'm missing some ingredients.
messages.story.service_availability.012: Hope it goes smoothly. We can try again once you've stocked up.
messages.story.service_availability.013: The district has suspended trading until I settle what's due, but you're welcome to sit with us.
messages.story.service_availability.014: No worries. Take your time sorting the paperwork. We can still sit here.
messages.story.inner_monologue.001: My eyes are closing. Maybe I should go upstairs and rest instead of fighting it.
messages.story.inner_monologue.002: When did I last eat? I'll make myself a bite before I carry on.
messages.story.inner_monologue.003: My head's crowded today. I'll stop and watch the water for a bit. Might clear my mind.
messages.story.inner_monologue.004: It's nice that sitting here doesn't ask me to hurry all the time.

messages.story.river_company.line_001: It’s nice having a spot away from all that traffic.
messages.story.river_company.line_002: I left the radio blaring back there. I’d rather listen to the water.
messages.story.river_company.line_003: See that boat out there? No hurry in the world.
messages.story.river_company.line_004: Wish my head would slow down like that.
messages.story.river_company.line_005: Cheers, mate. Sometimes you just need someone to listen.
messages.story.river_company.line_006: A few kind words can take the weight off a day.
messages.story.river_company.choice_002: What were you two talking about?
messages.story.river_company.line_007: Nothing much. The breeze, a bit of peace.
messages.story.river_company.line_008: And getting a breather after a long day.
messages.story.river_company.line_009: Let’s sit a little longer before life catches up with us.
messages.story.river_company.line_010: No rush. We’ve got a moment.

messages.ui.error.hospitality_save_requires_new_g: This save is from an earlier build. The hospitality update requires a new game; your old save has not been deleted.
messages.story.service_availability.015: I was going to ask for {order_label}... but honestly I don't have enough today. I feel awkward saying it.
messages.story.service_availability.016: Come on, this one is on me.
messages.story.service_availability.017: That's kind of you, my friend. I'll sit here and wait; take your time.
messages.story.service_availability.018: God provides. I'd be happy to make it for you.
messages.story.service_availability.019: Thank you. Your kindness means a lot today.
messages.story.service_availability.020: Don't worry about it. We're friends.
messages.story.service_availability.021: Thank you, my friend. I appreciate it.
messages.story.service_availability.022: Honestly, my friend, I'm stretched too, with rent and expenses to cover.
messages.story.service_availability.023: I understand. Don't worry about it. I'll just sit with you a while.
messages.story.service_availability.024: I'd like to make it for you, but I'm short of ingredients right now.
messages.story.service_availability.025: No worries. Sitting here with you is enough.
messages.story.service_availability.026: The council has paused the business until I settle the dues, but you're welcome to sit with us.
messages.story.service_availability.027: May things get easier for all of us. I'll sit here a while.
messages.story.visitors.hospitality_001: I still remember when you treated me. It wasn't just the food; your kindness stayed with me.
messages.story.visitors.hospitality_002: Remember when I told you I was short of money? I understand your situation. It hasn't changed our time together.
messages.topic.hospitality_memory: Remember our time here that day?
messages.ui.payment_unsettled: The {food} has already been served. Only payment remains to be settled.
messages.ui.payment_unsettled_promised: The {food} was served as promised. Confirm it as a treat with no payment.
messages.ui.payment_gift_settle: Record as a treat — no payment
messages.manual_topic.visitors/hospitality_memory: Remember our time here that day?
messages.story.companionship.exam_open: I have an exam coming up. I am breaking the studying into small bits instead of worrying about everything. Sitting here clears my head before I get back to the books.
messages.topic.exam_follow: How did your study plan go?
messages.story.companionship.exam_follow: Remember how I was splitting up the studying? I finished the bit I had been putting off and revised with a classmate. The exam is still ahead, but I feel calmer. I do not have to finish everything in one night.
messages.story.companionship.exam_ask: Youssef is not here today. If you run into him, could you ask how he is? Just let me know he is all right. I do not want to pester him.
messages.story.companionship.exam_ask.yes: If I see him, I will ask and pass on what he says.
messages.story.companionship.exam_ask.confirm: Thank you. Only when you have time; there is no hurry.
messages.story.companionship.exam_ask.later: I cannot promise. Let us take it easy.
messages.story.companionship.exam_ask.okay: Of course. We will catch up when we can.
messages.topic.exam_answer: Farid asked after you. What should I tell him?
messages.story.companionship.exam_answer: Farid asked after me? That is kind of you both. Tell him I am all right, revising for my exam, and feeling calmer with my study plan. I will stop by when I can, without promising a date.
messages.topic.exam_return: Tell Farid: Youssef is all right and studying
messages.story.companionship.exam_return: You saw Youssef and he told you that? Good, that is reassuring. Let him take his time studying. We will catch up when we can.
messages.topic.radio_open: What do you enjoy away from work?
messages.story.companionship.radio_open: I have an old radio from my father. I am trying to get its sound right in my own time. It is not a workshop job or an order for anyone, just something I like to sit with when I feel settled.
messages.story.companionship.radio_follow: The radio I told you about? I cleaned the contacts and the sound came back. There is still a little hiss, but I listened to an old song and enjoyed it. Not everything has to become new again.
messages.story.companionship.radio_ask: Has Farid not come today? If you see him, ask how he is. I have not sat with him for a while and would like to know he is all right.
messages.story.companionship.radio_ask.yes: If I see him, I will ask and pass on what he says.
messages.story.companionship.radio_ask.confirm: Thank you. Only when you have time; there is no hurry.
messages.story.companionship.radio_ask.later: I cannot promise. Let us take it easy.
messages.story.companionship.radio_ask.okay: Of course. We will catch up when we can.
messages.topic.radio_answer: Youssef asked after you. What should I pass on?
messages.story.companionship.radio_answer: Youssef asked? Tell him I am well and the old radio is singing again. If we run into each other, we can sit and talk, with no work appointment or obligation.
messages.topic.radio_return: Tell Youssef: Farid is well; the radio works
messages.story.companionship.radio_return: I am glad you saw Farid and let me know. That radio must have stories behind it. I will hear them from him when we meet. Thanks for passing that on.
messages.ui.error.stories_save_requires_new_game: This save is from an earlier build. Continuing stories and messages require a new game; your old files are preserved.
